g.text: Batch and streaming converge — and the one thing that does not
identical 4 windows · fix once, replay 9 · 1 window never final in streaming
seed: tools/stream_seed.js · total 45 · 4 windows
THE SAME MACHINERY, WITH AND WITHOUT AN ENDING
all four mechanisms are present in batch; three of them are trivial there
windows
4 either way: 19, 11, 7, 8
watermarks
bounded: jumps to "everything" at EOF · unbounded: advances with the data
triggers
bounded: fire once, at EOF · unbounded: early, on-time, late
accumulation
bounded: one pane, nothing to relate · unbounded: it matters
Batch does not lack watermarks — it has the easiest possible one, which reaches infinity when the file ends and closes every window at once.
Seeing it that way is what makes one codebase possible: you are not adding streaming machinery to a batch job, you are removing a special case.
Step 1/4 — batch is streaming over a bounded input
The reframing is the content of the claim. Batch has a watermark — the simplest one, which jumps to infinity at end of input — and a trigger,
which fires once. Three of the four mechanisms are trivial rather than absent, and recognising that is what lets one pipeline serve both modes
instead of two pipelines serving one each.
Batch and streaming converge — and the one thing that does not

seed: tools/stream_seed.js · total 45 · 4 windows
THE FIX, APPLIED ONCE
the whole correction, with no second implementation to keep in step
the wrong result
key "a" = 11, total 32
the fix
1 edit, in 1 pipeline
the replay
9 events through the corrected code
the corrected result
key "a" = 24, total 45 — and key "b" unchanged at 21
Key "b" reading 21 before and after is the check that the replay was faithful rather than merely different.
Under Lambda the same fix lands in 2 places and the two results have to be reconciled — which is where a second, subtler divergence usually
enters.
Step 2/4 — so one codebase, and Lambda's duplication disappears
The unaffected key is the useful detail: "b" reads 21 before and after the replay, which is how you know the replay reproduced history rather than
recomputing it differently. Under Lambda there is no such single check, because the two layers' outputs have to be reconciled before anything can
be verified.
Batch and streaming converge — and the one thing that does not

seed: tools/stream_seed.js · total 45 · 4 windows
THE LOG IS THE TRUTH; THE PIPELINE IS DISPOSABLE
one mechanism serves logic changes, bug fixes and new consumers
changing business logic
deploy the new pipeline, replay 9 events
fixing a bug
the same operation — nothing special about a correction
adding a new output
also the same operation, over the same log
so the pipeline is
disposable; the log is what must not be lost
This is ch06's duality as an operational practice: the state is a function of the log, so it can be discarded and rebuilt rather than migrated.
Which inverts the usual anxiety — the risky asset is not the pipeline you are about to replace, it is the log you are assuming is still complete.
Step 3/4 — reprocessing becomes a first-class operation
Three different kinds of change collapse into one operation, which is what "first-class" means here: a bug fix, a logic change and a new consumer
are all "replay the log through new code". The consequence worth internalising is the inversion in the note — the pipeline becomes the cheap,
replaceable part, and the log becomes the thing you cannot afford to lose.

WHAT THE MODEL DOES NOT UNIFY
identical values, and one column where they differ
batch: final at event 9 · streaming: final after event 4
batch: final at event 9 · streaming: final after event 8
batch: final at event 9 · streaming: final after event 8
batch: final at event 9 · streaming: NEVER final
1 of the 4 windows is final in batch and never final in streaming — holding 8, with every one of its events already received.
The model unifies the HOW. It does not make an unbounded input end, and that is not a gap in the model — it is the thing the model is about.
Step 4/4 — and what stays distinct: streams do not end
The honest limit of the convergence, with a number on it: window [12:08, 12:10) holds 8, has received all of its events, and is final under batch
while never final under streaming. The model unifies the computation and the vocabulary; it does not give an unbounded stream an ending.
